business: Yu Chun Korean Restaurant (sit-down Korean restaurant known for chik naengmyeon, arrowroot black noodles)
why_not: Ice-cold noodles sound great on a hot day, but $18.95 for a bowl that won't fill me up means adding mandoo or a stew, and with tax and tip I'm near $50 for one person. On a week in Waikiki where every meal already costs too much, I'd pick somewhere I can eat a full meal for less.

When I book dinner for the family, kalbi at $38.95 a plate plus the automatic 20% tip for five or more adds up quickly. I can get naengmyeon and BBQ for the group cheaper on Keeaumoku St, where we already go.
I already have my Korean place on Keeaumoku and I eat Yu Chun-style naengmyeon back home in Japan, so on a short trip I'd rather go where I know or try something I can't get at home.
When family's in town I take them to my usual Korean place on Keeaumoku, they know me there and I know what I'm getting. Nineteen bucks for cold noodles isn't going to pull me off that.
why_yes: I know the Yu Chun name and chik naengmyeon in cold broth is exactly what I want on a hot Honolulu day near Ala Moana, so I would go once on this trip if the recent Google and Yelp reviews and photos hold up. I am only here for a short stay, so one visit, maybe two at most.

I know the Yu Chun name, and black arrowroot chik naengmyeon is exactly the kind of dish I cannot get easily at home, so I would go once during my five days. I would order the spicy raw fish version and add mandoo or bulgogi so I leave full.
I'm in Honolulu, it's hot, and real chik naengmyeon with arrowroot noodles is exactly what I go looking for. I'd grumble about the price, but I'd go, and probably go back once more before I fly home.

When family comes in from out of town I need somewhere close to Ala Moana for a real Korean meal, and a bowl of naengmyeon under twenty dollars is fair for Honolulu. I would go once, but I would steer everyone to the noodles and share one kalbi, not order kalbi for everybody.
I know the Yu Chun name and I crave cold naengmyeon on a hot day, so I would go once on this trip. I would order the $18.95 bowl and maybe mandoo, not the kalbi.

Chewy arrowroot naengmyeon in ice-cold broth is exactly what I crave on a hot day, and it's an easy place to take visiting family near Ala Moana. $18.95 is a bit much for noodles, but for the real thing I'll pay it.

Yu Chun is in my guidebook and all over the Instagram posts I saved, and ice-cold naengmyeon on a hot Honolulu afternoon is exactly what I want. It is near Ala Moana, where I am shopping anyway, so I will go once on this trip.

It's right by Ala Moana where I already am on weekends, and chik naengmyeon isn't something every place does, so I'd try it once if the Yelp photos look good. But at $18.95 plus tax and tip it's not becoming my regular when Keeaumoku is right there for less.
